summary: Full-extraction pass over 20 stored Vanuatu documents (citizenship laws and orders, Citizenship Office letters and web pages, FIU notice, IMF 2015/2016/2023 Article IV reports). Adds remaining programme prices and conditions, statutory decision deadlines, IMF 2024-2028 projections of citizenship revenue, IMF 2015 worldwide programme table, and a few dated events.

observations.location: PDF p. 4 (printed p. 3), Schedule item 5, s.13CA(2)
observations.quote: Citizenship may be granted within 3 months if the investor under subsection (1) pays the prescribed fee under the Real Estate Option Program.
observations.notes: Statutory time limit for the first REO route (s.13CA, in force 8 Jul 2014, repealed by Act No. 40 of 2014 from 23 Jan 2015); "may be granted within", a legal target, not a measured processing time.

observations.location: PDF p. 5 (printed p. 4), Schedule item 13, s.13C(3)
observations.quote: The Commission is to approve and grant a citizenship within 3 months of receiving an application under this section.
observations.notes: Statutory decision deadline (a legal target), not a measured processing time. Act No. 40 of 2014, in force 23 Jan 2015.

observations.location: PDF p. 3, Schedule, s.13E(4) (OCR)
observations.quote: The Commission must within 3 months of receiving an application under this section, make a decision on whether or not to approve and grant a citizenship.
observations.notes: Statutory decision deadline (a legal target), not a measured processing time. Act No. 34 of 2018, in force 7 Jan 2019. Quote from OCR of the scanned page.

observations.location: news item "CIIP suspension removed", para 2
observations.quote: The Citizenship Commission has granted approved of three (3) agents to operate the Capital Investment Immigration Plan (CIIP)

program_terms.applies_to: investor (standard route: compliance with the CIIP residence-permit plan before citizenship)
program_terms.location: PDF p. 8 (printed p. 7), Schedule item 9, s.13C(1)(a)
program_terms.quote: the investor complies with the requirements of the Capital Investment Immigration Plan for a period of 24 months
program_terms.notes: Counted from the date the investor applied for a residence permit under Immigration Visa Regulation No. 180 of 2011. Section 13C was replaced by Act No. 40 of 2014 (in force 23 Jan 2015).

program_terms.applies_to: investor applying within 9 months of the residence-permit application (fast route)
program_terms.location: PDF pp. 8-9 (printed pp. 7-8), Schedule item 9, s.13C(1)(b)
program_terms.quote: donates to the Vanuatu Government a further 25% of his or her investment made under the Plan
program_terms.notes: Fast route conditions: apply within 9 months of the residence-permit application, stay compliant with the Plan, waive repayment of the government bonds issued under the Plan, and donate a further 25% of the investment. Replaced by Act No. 40 of 2014.

program_terms.applies_to: first 500 applicants, citizenship granted within 3 months after approval
program_terms.location: PDF p. 9 (printed p. 8), Schedule item 9, s.13C(2)-(3)
program_terms.quote: If an application is granted within the period stated in subsection (2), the investor waives 50% of his or her investment made under the Plan.
program_terms.notes: s.13C(2): "for the first 500 applicants -citizenship will be granted within 3 months after an application has been approved by the Commission". Replaced by Act No. 40 of 2014.

program_terms.location: PDF p. 2, Schedule item 1, new clause 3A (OCR)

program_terms.notes: A minimum sales quota for agents, not a cost to applicants. Quote from OCR of the scanned order.

program_terms.applies_to: married couple
program_terms.quote: for a married couple —the selling price must not be less than 150,000USD
program_terms.notes: Minimum price designated agents must charge. Quote from OCR.

program_terms.quote: for a married couple and a child under 18 years of age -the selling price must not be less than 165,000USD

program_terms.applies_to: each additional child
program_terms.notes: Prescribed fee payable to the government account. Quote from OCR.

program_terms.applies_to: each additional resident dependant (child aged 18-25 in full-time education, or parent over 50)
program_terms.notes: Prescribed fee payable to the government account; resident dependant defined in clause 1. Quote from OCR.

program_terms.applies_to: applicant, paid before the Commission considers the application
program_terms.quote: an applicant must pay 25% of the prescribed fee due under his or her application before the Commission considers his or her application
program_terms.notes: The 25% is not refundable if the application is refused (clause 6(4)(b)); the remaining 75% is due before the certificate is issued; 100% may be paid upfront. Quote from OCR.

program_terms.applies_to: applicant, paid before the certificate of citizenship is issued
program_terms.quote: an applicant must pay 75% of the prescribed fee due under his or her application before the Commission issues the certificate of citizenship to him or her.
program_terms.notes: Quote from OCR.

program_terms.applies_to: VERP citizen applying for spouse and a child or 2 children
program_terms.quote: the person must pay an administration fee of USD5,000 to process the application.
program_terms.notes: Set by the DSP Regulations for family members of people who obtained citizenship under the VERP. Amount read as USD5,000 from a 500 dpi OCR (300 dpi OCR read "USDS,000").

program_terms.applies_to: Honorary Citizenship DSP citizen granted before the Order No. 94 of 2018 fee reduction, applying for spouse and a child or 2 children
program_terms.quote: the person must pay an administration fee of USD5,000 to process the application.
program_terms.notes: Amount read as USD5,000 from a 500 dpi OCR (300 dpi OCR read "USDS,000").

program_terms.applies_to: Honorary Citizenship DSP citizen granted after the Order No. 94 of 2018 fee reduction, applying for spouse and a child or 2 children (plus the difference to the new prescribed fee)
program_terms.quote: the person must pay an administration fee of USD 5000 and the difference between the amount paid on the first application and the new fees prescribed under subclause 7(1).
program_terms.notes: Quote from OCR.

program_terms.applies_to: child born after the parent was granted citizenship under the Honorary Citizenship DSP or VERP
program_terms.quote: The child is to pay a passport fee of VT 10,000.
program_terms.notes: Quote from OCR.

program_terms.applies_to: applicant from a restricted country (must not have resided there for the last 5 years and must show permanent residency abroad)
program_terms.quote: has not resided in the restricted country for the last 5 years
program_terms.notes: Eligibility condition, not a cost. The restricted countries are not listed in the Order. Quote from OCR.

program_terms.applies_to: each new certificate after loss or damage due to the bearer's negligence
program_terms.quote: event of a lost or damage Certificate done due to the bearers negligence
program_terms.notes: The schedule prints "VT600,000 | USD6,000" for this item. Quote from OCR.

events.title: Act No. 8 of 2016 rewrites the CIIP and Contribution Program sections
events.description: The 2021 consolidation records that sections 13C (CIIP) and 13D (Contribution Program) were substituted by Act No. 8 of 2016; in the consolidated text the prescribed fees under both cover the applicant, spouse and 2 children, with a decision due within 3 months.
events.location: PDF p. 15, endnotes; PDF p. 9, s.13C-13D (OCR)

events.title: Act No. 1 of 2021 inserts the Real Estate Option Program section (s.13F)
events.description: The 2021 consolidation records that section 13F, the legal basis of the current Real Estate Option Program, was inserted by Act No. 1 of 2021.

events.title: Switzerland suspends visa waiver for recent Vanuatu passports
events.description: The IMF reports that in 2022 the EU and Switzerland suspended visa waiver agreements for Vanuatu passports issued after May 2015.
events.location: PDF p. 98, DSA para 7; PDF p. 9, para 2
events.quote: the EU and Switzerland suspended in 2022 visa waiver agreements for Vanuatu passports issued after May 2015

events.title: EU delays full visa waiver suspension to August 2024 (IMF account)
events.description: The IMF states that in February 2023 the EU agreed to delay converting the partial suspension into a full suspension for all Vanuatu passport holders until August 2024, an 18-month extension to enact reforms. This differs from EU legal acts already in the timeline (full suspension decided November 2022); kept as the IMF's account.
events.location: PDF p. 9, para 2; PDF p. 23, ECP bullet and footnote 27
events.quote: In February 2023, the EU agreed to delay converting the partial suspension to a full suspension (for all Vanuatu passport holders) until August 2024

ledger.contains: Amending Act (in force 21 Jan 2014): reconstitutes the Citizenship Commission, Secretary General and Internal Screening Committee, Bislama test for naturalisation, Part 3A dual citizenship with the CIIP investor route (s.13B-13D: 24-month plan compliance or fast route within 9 months with bond-repayment waiver and a further 25% donation; first 500 applicants granted within 3 months of approval and waive 50% of investment), honorary citizenship (s.20), offences (fines VT1,000,000 for facilitating unlawful grants, VT2,000,000 for bribery; general offence fine raised from 75,000 to 1,000,000). Penalties and Commission meeting limits are general, not programme numbers, and are not tabled. CIIP launch event already recorded.

Amending Act (in force 8 Jul 2014) adding the first Real Estate Option route (s.13CA): residence visa under Immigration Visa Regulation No. 180 of 2011, investment of the "prescribed amount" (not stated) in a lot in a Vanuatu Government Approved Project held via a local company, grant within 3 months on payment of the prescribed fee. No amounts printed. Event already recorded.

Amending Act (in force 23 Jan 2015): Commission meetings (12 ordinary, 4 extraordinary a year), approval lapses unless the citizenship fee is paid and oath taken within 3 months (2-month extension possible), new character bars, applications for unnamed children, CIIP rules delegated to regulation with the fee covering applicant, spouse and 1 child, CIIP decision within 3 months, repeal of the first REO route (s.13CA), new offence for fraudulently obtained citizenship (fine up to VT5,000,000 or 10 years). The general penalty and meeting numbers are not programme numbers. Event already recorded.

Amending Act (in force 7 Jan 2019), English and French: inserts s.13E giving the Development Support Program a statutory basis; fees set by regulation cover applicant, spouse and 2 children; extra fees may be prescribed for other children or resident dependants; decision within 3 months. No amounts. Event already recorded.

Consolidated Citizenship Act (2021 edition, scanned, read by OCR): Commission, Secretary General and screening committee; naturalisation; Part 3A dual citizenship with investor routes CIIP (s.13C), Contribution Program (s.13D), DSP (s.13E) and REO (s.13F), each with fees set by regulation covering applicant, spouse and 2 children and a 3-month decision deadline; loss, deprivation, renunciation; offences (fines VT1,000,000 to VT5,000,000, general, not tabled); fee-making powers; amendment endnotes. No programme amounts. Statutory deadlines and the two dated amendments (Act 8 of 2016, Act 1 of 2021) taken.

Citizenship Office directive of 30 April 2020 to DSP and VCP agents restating the prescribed government minimum contribution and minimum selling price for four family categories under Regulation Orders 33 and 34 of 2019, warning that agents underselling risk licence cancellation and applicants risk revocation. All 16 prices now recorded (DSP and VCP); event already recorded.

Citizenship Commission press release, 2 Dec 2024: reaction to EU visa decision, enhanced FIU/Interpol/Immigration due diligence, CIIP mandatory USD 50,000 investment component, biometric passports (capture systems abroad by March 2025, not programme-specific), agent agreements to lapse by January 2025. USD 50,000 term and reform event already recorded; nothing else in scope.

Citizenship Office letter of 26 Aug 2021 on the commencement of the REO Program: legal basis (s.13F, Regulation Order No. 93 of 2021), property purchase in a Vanuatu Government Approved Project plus prescribed fees (amounts not given), the four approved projects by name, applications via the Master Agent. Number of approved projects taken.
Undated Citizenship Office news item: CIIP suspension lifted "as of 21 March 2016"; Commission approved three agents to operate the CIIP under "Order 93 of 2023". Agent count taken.
ledger.to_do: Decision needed: whether to record the CIIP suspension lift dated 21 March 2016 as an event. The page prints that date, but the earlier pass left it out because it does not fit the "Order 93 of 2023" reference on the same page.

ledger.contains: Undated Citizenship Office news item: REO program commenced 23 July 2021; property in a Vanuatu Government Approved Project plus prescribed fees; 4 approved projects listed by name. Launch event already recorded; project count taken.

Undated Citizenship Office news item: the current Commission has revoked "around almost 30" citizenships granted contrary to the Act and Constitution. Already recorded (citizenships_revoked, claim); nothing else in scope.

Citizenship Office web page listing the types of citizenship granted (naturalisation, marriage, entitlement, regain, CIIP Form D, honorary citizenship under the DSP, VCP, REO). No numbers, prices or dates.

DSP (Amendment) Regulations Order No. 39 of 2020 (27 Mar 2020): agent quota of at least 12 investors a year, due diligence by an international specialist firm plus the FIU, FIU time limit changed from 48 to 96 hours (procedural, not tabled), due diligence fee USD2,000 to USD5,000. Fee change and event already recorded; agent quota taken.

DSP Regulations Order No. 33 of 2019 (24 Apr 2019): definitions; agents must be Vanuatu citizens based in Port Vila; minimum selling prices for four family categories (USD 130,000-180,000); application procedure (FIU check within 48 hours, notice of decisions within 48 hours, certificate within 90 days of approval, agent change after 6 months: procedural deadlines, described here, not tabled); payment in tranches 25%/75%; applicants from restricted countries; prescribed fees USD 80,000-130,000 plus USD 10,000 per extra child or resident dependant; VT5000 application fee, VT10,000 certificate fee, USD2,000 due diligence; USD5,000 administration fees for families of VERP and earlier DSP citizens; VT10,000 passport fee for children born later. All amounts now recorded.

Citizenship fees order of 20 Sep 2013 replacing the 1985 schedules: application form fees (Form A VT5,000 / VT7,000, B and C VT5,000, Form D VT10,000) and certificate fees for naturalisation, marriage, entitlement and status certificates (VT30,000-600,000), register search fees. Only Form D (investor) concerns the programme and is already recorded; the rest are ordinary naturalisation fees, out of scope.

Citizenship fees order of 30 Jan 2014: Form D (CIIP) application fee VT25,000 / USD250; ordinary certificate fee changes for children and married persons (out of scope); new Schedule 5 CIIP certificate fees: VT1,000,000 / USD10,000 per certificate for applicant and family, VT600,000 / USD6,000 for a replacement. CIIP fees now all recorded (in vatu; USD equivalents in quotes and notes).

FIU notice of 14 Jan 2025 on new due diligence procedures for DSP, CIIP and VCP files from 16 Jan 2025 (documents required incl. passport valid more than 6 months, email submission, 2 new staff, weekly internal screening committee). Event already recorded; no programme numbers.

IMF 2015 Article IV and RCF/RFI request (post-Cyclone Pam). In scope: para 10-11 (HKPR and CIIP revenue 1.3% of GDP in 2014; HKPR suspension leaves a 1.1% of GDP shortfall in 2015 budget), para on revenue mobilisation, Appendix III on economic citizenship (Table 1 of minimum investment, residency requirement and qualifying period for 24 programmes worldwide; 1990s passport sales; HKPR and CIIP terms and revenue; St Kitts 13% of GDP in 2013), p. 53 footnote (1,706 international companies registered through Hong Kong by 2013, company registry, not programme). Rest is general macro, fiscal, banking and cyclone material. Taken: HKPR 2015 budget, St Kitts 2013 share, HKPR investment, all printed numbers in Table 1 (investment, residency days/months, qualifying years); words such as "No", "Immediate" and "One year" not converted.

ledger.contains: IMF 2016 Article IV staff report: macro, fiscal, financial and post-Cyclone Pam material. Programme content is one sentence (para 16): 2016 domestic revenue expected to rise, supported by receipts from the Citizenship Program and the Vanuatu Economic Rehabilitation Program "launched in late 2015" (no numbers; launch dating already in the VERP programme notes). Statistical tables have no citizenship lines (only "Other revenue").

IMF 2023 Article IV staff report. In scope: ECP revenue in Table 2 (2019-2028, millions of vatu and percent of GDP), down 27% y/y in 2022 (fn 5), severe downside scenario text table (baseline 7.5/4.6/4.2% of GDP for 2022/2024/2027; downside assumes 0.0 from 2023: an assumption, not taken), ECP 33% of total revenue in 2020 (RAM) and "one third" in 2021 (DSA, words, not converted), EBA-lite windfall adjustment -1.0% of GDP (model parameter, not taken), ECP cost footnote (USD 135,000-185,000, government share 80,000-130,000), EU/Swiss visa waiver suspension and EU delay, governance issues, correspondent banking loss 2021, debt prepayments financed by ECP revenue (VUV 2 billion in 2021, total prepayment, not ECP money). Rest is macro, banking, digital money, tax policy and DSA material. Taken: 2024-2028 projections, 2022 change, family-of-four and government-share prices, two visa events.
